reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) from a single study on HEB-Ta composites directly supports the formation of a viscous, protective Ta2O5-B2O3 glassy layer that fills defects and reduces oxidation. However, the evidence is for bulk ceramic composites, not a thin Ta coating on a NiCoCrAl alloy, so the premise that this mechanism will occur and be effective in the proposed coated alloy system is an extrapolation not directly supported by the cited passages.
premises: Ta oxidizes to Ta2O5 and interacts with B2O3 to form a viscous glassy layer
The Ta2O5-B2O3 glassy layer fills pores and defects, forming a dense oxide layer
This dense glassy layer reduces oxygen diffusion and enhances oxidation resistance
The protective effect is observed at high temperatures (up to 1400 °C) in Ta-containing systems
